reviews.text: Doctors are mostly okay but this is one of the consistently worst offices I've been to. They make me wait more than a half hour each time after my appointment was made while a parade of chaotic animals frightens my pet for better part of an hour. As I type this someone is in the office complaining that they messed up an appointment and now his dog is suffering. Ridiculous

Iv been coming here with my babies for over 5 years.

PROS: The office is pretty clean. Every doctor I have in countered has been extremely professional, excellent bedside manner and has  truly showed me they cared.

Cons: the front desk is very unprofessional most of the time but not all the time. I experienced it towards myself and when I sat in the lobby I witnessed it with someone else they were in the phone with and in person! When you call with an issue the staff is not very friendly or that helpful. Their main concern is how long has it been since the last time you were there. Example: I called on 10/03/2026 a lady answered the phone, I said “hello can you have a doctor give me a call because my baby/dog hasn’t peed since yesterday. She asked for my phone number then she came back and said you were here yesterday? I said “No”  she said with an attitude you said you are here yesterday , I said “No I did not say that I said my dog hasn’t peed since yesterday. With more attitude she said well Diamond hasn’t been here since May so she’s going to require an examination. I said so your saying she’s fine until then, ? She said “ no she needs to be seen. She never offered me to come in right away or that  I needed to take her to Urgent care right away or the hospital! Also in my
Opinion If my pets are patient there and they’re up-to-date with their physicals, why can’t a doctor at least call me back to hear what’s going on and give me options of what to do until they can be seen not a receptionist at the front desk who is unprofessional!! I’ve experienced this on more than one occasion with the front desks unprofessionalism! I also noticed they pay a little favoritism as well at times the only thing that keeps me coming back like I said are the doctors they are  really good, however, I’m just a little bit over the rest of the staff and it’s making me feel like I might need to find a new vet clinic

I cannot say enough about how amazing Dr. Alex Collada is. Not only would I travel a million miles for him, he is just genuinely kind. Thank you Caitlyn and Terria for making us feel welcomed (Doggy 🥣 Water Bowl).

When you know you know! He will never give your dog or recommend anything, If not completely necessary.  In other words, he's not about the money. Very importantly people moving forward, you're not going to get ripped off.

He listens, his staff cares. I highly recommend Alex as a professional and a kind man. He definitely is in his element. He absolutely adores animals.

Trust me, when I say he's worth traveling to. We recommend him to everyone in our business as well. Annodam Wellness/ Doylestown, PA -  as a matter of fact, a lot of our clients have said they will make the travel to him. □

This review is from our hearts. We appreciate you Alex and you always go above and beyond. Thank you.♡
I love you to the beach and back!!!!!

I cannot recommend Queen Village Animal Hospital enough. The quality of care is 100% worth the price.

I brought my geriatric cat Serra here for a decade. I truly believe she made it into her 20s because of the calm, kind and professional care of these veterinarians.

I would like to give huge thanks and praise to Vets Collada and Goldner for handling Serra's declining health with compassion, while being realistic and supportive. They never tried to talk me into unnecessary services or make me feel like I was overreacting. The support and reassurance I got from them was so crucial during Serra's last years.

Your pet will be in good hands if you choose this place.

Stay away from Queens Village Animal Hospital. They completely ignore explicit written intake directives, fail to maintain basic post-operative staffing safety protocols, and execute massive unauthorized procedures.

I brought my 12-year-old, 6 lb senior Maltese, Fifi, in for a dental procedure. On the mandatory intake form, I explicitly checked the box: "NO, I DO NOT authorize extractions without being contacted first." They completely violated this directive. Based on a brief status update phone call while my dog was already incapacitated under anesthesia, they performed a massive, unauthorized 12-tooth extraction and demanded $1,908 based entirely on an unsigned internal worksheet.

The billing practices are deceptive, but their post-operative abandonment is terrifying:

Gross Abandonment: This facility left the building completely unstaffed by doctors or trained technicians after major surgeries. I notified them I was coming an hour early and walked into an empty facility where my recovering senior dog was left completely unmonitored and in visible physical distress in a back room. Had I not arrived early, she would have sat abandoned for hours with zero clinical monitoring of her airway or vitals following invasive oral surgery.

Pet Withheld for Payment: Despite the empty building and my dog's clear suffering, the front desk refused to retrieve her from the back room until a transaction was successfully processed.

Concealed Pre-Op Trauma: Only after taking my money did they bring her out, completely failing to return the comfort blanket I brought from home. When I demanded my property, a staff member casually admitted that my dog was in such extreme physiological distress before the surgery that she severely fouled herself (feces, urine, and vomit) and required a bath. Proceeding with elective general anesthesia on a completely destabilized, traumatized 6 lb senior pet violates standard safety protocols.

To top off this severe negligence, they sent her home with zero post-operative mouth protection (no cone). Due to their substandard post-op care and the environment she was left in, Fifi developed a severe, painful bacterial infection around her mouth (mucocutaneous pyoderma). I had to rush her to Pennsauken Animal Hospital, where an independent veterinarian had to put her on a heavy 14-day course of antibiotics to fix Queens Village’s medical failure.

They issued a partial refund only after a formal dispute was initiated, but a minor credit does not clear their record. This business operates with an arrogant disregard for consumer consent, post-op safety, and basic animal welfare. Do not trust them with an animal you care about. This complaint is going to all oversight agencies!  May 27 , 2026

UPDATE...my dog had to go to an emergency appointment at another vet hospital for severe infection as a result of poor aftercare at Queens Village. She was given another 2 week round of antibiotics and wore a cone collar. During that exam the Dr noted that the remaining teeth were not touched. So, they never did the dental cleaning : just went straight to ripping her mouth apart. Also , did not administer her rabies vax while she was there. That is a state mandate!!

I was a client for over 10 years. Something changed in that practice . DISGRACEFUL!!!

UPDATE: Another trip to the hospital for yet more infection because bacteria was left in the mouth from NOT doing the proper procedure .  This means my dog has been medicated since March . Who does this to a 5lb senior dog?!

DISGRACE!!

In person visit with hopes to get a treatment for my dog. Very vague answers to specific questions/issues and a lot of assumptions instead of a medical diagnosis. It felt like I was talking with one of my friends who also has a dog and not an actual vet. Not recommended.
We've been taking our dog here for years and have always had a great experience. Dr. Goldner is a truly outstanding clinician—knowledgeable, thorough, and clearly deeply committed to animal care.

Compassionate, knowledgeable staff and clean, well-run clinic. Appointments aren’t rushed, front desk staff are friendly and responsive, and appointments are easy to schedule. While they’re often busy, operations are efficient with little to no wait time. Dr. Suzanne Hange is especially wonderful. My dog was born with physical anomalies resulting in symptoms that were challenging to diagnose. Dr. Hange got to the root of his issues and clearly explained his condition. I appreciate her suggesting minimally invasive treatment as a first step over more aggressive options. High standard of care and highly recommended!

I didn’t have to wait at all, and they were very kind to my dog during the vaccination process. They even had peanut butter, which helped a lot. The technician clearly loves animals, and my dog didn’t seem to be in pain after the vaccine like he has been during vaccines in the past

It's the best veterinary hospital all the staff are very kind and welcoming
I want to thank Dr. Alexander Collazo, without a doubt the best veterinarian. Thank you for treating my cat Mustache with such gentleness and love.

My perspective on Queen Village Animal Hospital is unique: I have been a loyal client for years and also a long-time member of their staff. While my commitment to this practice is clear, the reason behind it is simply the unmatched quality of care provided here.
The veterinarians at Queen Village are defined by their compassion, skilled expertise, and genuine love for animals. Not to mention that they are just really good people outside of the hospital too. How many people can say they truly love the people they work for? I can.
My pets have benefited from their exceptional treatment across every stage of life. The doctors here have gone above and beyond- they have prolonged my pets’ lives, dramatically improved their quality of life, and, in critical moments, saved them.
Though I have experience with many excellent ERs and specialty practices, I can confidently say the dedicated, meticulous treatment offered by the Queen Village doctors is unparalleled. For me, they are nothing short of true veterinary superheroes. If your pets are your family, this is where you need to bring them.

If I could give no stars to this veterinary clinic in PHILADELPHIA on BAINBRIDGE STREET, I most assuredly would. I brought my new puppy, Gretel, in to be seen as she had an allergic reaction to what turned out to be nylon. I was very upset and asking a lot of questions during my first consultation. On my follow-up visit, they left me in a room to wait for the vet. When the veterinarian came in and opened Gretel's file, they had forgotten to remove the sticky note affixed to the top page that had the  word "nut job" written on it. I most assuredly brought Gretel to this veterinary practice for the first time in 2006. They also sent me a postcard thanking me for bringing my cat, Abigail, into their practice and that they hoped to see her again soon. I brought my cat into their practice b/c she had to be put sleep due to severe health issues. I lived just around the corner on 4th and South Streets from 2005 - 2009. Their response is a complete lie.

It does NOT matter where my reviews are based NOW. This is where I live NOW. I lived in PHILADELPHIA for MANY years as I noted in my review. I don't expect you to take ANY accountability for your unprofessional behavior. You didn't THEN, why should you now? NEW management and new owners are too very different things. HERE is your accountability. Your response should have started with nothing less than "I am sorry for your experience..." The lack of professionalism has not improved new management or not!!!!

I am not a client of yours now, b/c:

• Your client services were egregious
• I no longer live in the state

Neither of these reasons negate my ability to communicate my experience or review your services. If you are unhappy with the review, you fix that by doing better and apologizing - not trying to make excuses for the behavior. After all, your practice name has NOT changed. That makes you culpable for all experiences that happened under the practice name alone.

And, to be very clear, I live in NYC, NOT Woodside NY. Your practice "QUEENS VILLAGE ANIMAL HOSPITAL" is called that, b/c you are located in Queens Village, Philadelphia, PA. 4th and South Streets are just around the corner from your practice and LESS than a five minute walk.

Being in the petcare industry for 22 years and owning my own business for more than 12 years, I have  graciously shared this review, experience, and your practice name with my 30k+ followers in the tri-state area.

Now, you have a very good day and take some time to think about how you can elevate your services, embrace and have empathy for a diverse group of clients, and learn what it means to take responsibility for unprofessional, thoughtless, and hurtful behavior.

I'm really sorry I dont remember her name, but the last vet I saw was absolutely wonderful! The Asian lady. I felt really heard and she was so compassionate. All the vet techs are great too! The only reason why I'm switching vet hospitals is because I found a much closer one which will make the travel way less stressful for me and Suki since I'm without a car🙏🏼 I wanted to leave a review so the vet knows it's nothing against her or the clinic -- I'm simply switching due to travel distance. I had already made an appointment with the new vet before coming in. I knocked off a star because the front desk staff were not the friendliest in my few interactions with them.
They are always friendly and accommodating for my nervous Great Dane. Recommended for anyone who lives in the area.

One of the best animal hospitals ! The staff is amazing…very caring, compassionate and always willing to work with you when it comes to the health and care of your fur babies 🥰🥰🥰 highly recommend Queen Village Animal Hospital

1. Brought my kitten here because he was coughing the vet dismissed us saying the kitten is fine. My kitten keeps coughing 3-4 times a day, struggling to breathe. I asked for X-rays, vet said they don’t recommend & and it’s most likely allergies. Called them back in a week coz he kept coughing, they say I’d have to pay for another exam even though he just got an exam. They just trying to get as much money as possible and are not concerned about actually helping my pet.

2.Rude front desk. Called to find out about possible ways to diagnose my kitten and was dismissed saying she’s the only person in the hospital and has other clients. I guess my kitten is not as important.

Update: took my kitten to a different vet, they scanned his lungs and found pneumonia. They said the more I wait the worse it gets. So this clinic proved once again to be unreliable. Would not trust my pet with them ever again.
Love this place!

Second edit: I do not recommend getting a health certificate for travel to the UK from Queen Village. Go to another provider. I had a bad experience and did not feel heard and felt that many issues arose because the staff weren’t prepared or thinking ahead. The USDA makes changes to their requirements every 4-6 months and apparently one of these new requirements came up the week of my appointment so there was lots of scrambling to accommodate the new requirements. The team were extremely responsive however I just have to believe there is a better way.. they need to proactively find out the usda requirements sooner and not put that stress on themselves and customers or blame the operating times of other vets for the issues. I was prescribed gabapentin twice and then told i couldnt use it on the travel (they did say they would refund this part) and also asked me to bike to my previous vet to collect records of a past vaccine because they didnt think to ask for them months earlier when I originally asked about the process. Long story short was hard to trust the staff as much of the required info could have been gathered in advance if there had been more care. Though they are extremely well meaning and responsive, it was still much more stressful than it needed to be and they ultimately failed to provide expertise in filling out the usda form that i required, in multiple areas meaning there was a chance my cat would have issues at customs. I was denied a refund. I had to use ink pen over a photocopy in order to meet the requirements for a wet ink vaccine record.

Original review- Came here because my regular vet was shut. I was initially stressed by the high bills that were involved to new patients so i do recommended asking about costs before going in so they can explain as they go. After Dr Holden helped explain costs and methods for care to me, I felt so much better. He shared which treatments he recommended and offered insight about benefits of each treatment. He made a scary trip much better. Thank you.

Queen Village Animal Hospital is the best. The front desk staff and vet techs are so kind and helpful. Dr. Hange is amazing - she is able to handle my large, goofy, and sometimes difficult pup with ease. Could not recommend more highly!

I have had mixed experiences at this location, but I am writing this review to specifically thank Jess at the front desk and Dr. Hange for getting me through an aggression incident with my cat. They were able to fit us in for a same-day appointment, and Jess especially went above and beyond to offer help during an extremely stressful day.

We went to a different vet prior and never really felt cared about. Queen Village Animal Hospital is the complete opposite - they really care about our pup Hoagie and do whatever they can to fix whatever ailments he comes in with. He is a very shy guy, and they're extremely patient with him and do their best to make him feel very comfortable. Thankful for the vet and the staff here!

I can’t say enough good things about this place. They’re caring, compassionate and truly care about my pup. They’re quick to answer questions I have whether I’m at an appointment or emailing them questions over the weekend.

I’m so grateful for Queen Village Animal Hospital (and Dr. Greiner and Dr. Hange, particularly!).

Unprofessional. The tech tried to pick up my terrified pup, even when the medicine they had to "administer" was just squirting something in her mouth (that I could easily do). My dog snapped at her - did not bite. The tech Never asked if she could pick her up- it felt like she didn't know what she was doing.

This happened a while ago and I thought it was squashed but the next 2 times my dog went for an appointment they say she's a biter? Even as far as saying she has a Scarlet letter? This really just adds insult to injury since I feel like they were bad at their job and caused the incident.

One rude comment I can forgive but 2 times making us feel bad about it is the last straw. I should mention that I think my dogs fear of the vet started when they "expressed" her when she didn't even need it (it was just allergies). I heard her scream from the lobby. so sad and scary.

At this point I don't trust them and their customer service is bad. Front desk person always seems mad.

I used to go to pet mechanic in south but they closed so I went to QVAH in a bind. Never again!

Lol update - my chewy order accidentally sent my dogs prescription here and they denied it and emailed me saying we have been kicked out of using them. Much better solution than saying sorry and trying to be better. Good luck QVAH - killing it 😂
Great vets. So caring and loving.the best experience for my dog. No trauma.

I’ve been coming here for nearly a decade and have so many positive things to say about QVAH. Dr. Greiner is so kind, compassionate, and professional. I appreciate that she gives options without judgment and is realistic about expectations while also easing my anxiety. The staff and vet techs have been wonderful with our various babies - reactive pittie, very annoyed cat, anxious mastiff, and now happy lab puppy. We moved to a different neighborhood and I still make the trek there! I don’t trust anyone else with our fur babies. Can’t recommend enough.

This is hands down some of the best service you will get for your fur babies. The Dr literally got on the ground and crawled around after our cat to make her feel comfortable and greet her at her level, and it worked! Vs going to other places and our cat freaking out picking up on the Drs terrible energy. Unfortunately, they are a bit on the costly side, (It really depends on what kind of medication you are buying and the situation) but honestly, it’s with good reason. Best service you can get. Quick and efficient.

10/10 animal hospital and I’m picky, and a harsh critic at times. I had a happy shocked face when they told me my (cheap) total for payment. They were kind on my pockets. I brought my sick cat here after taking him to an emergency vet (blue pearl) and he was handled with such care and love. The doctor was able to comfort me, and my baby with education and kindness about what’s going on. Blue pearl didn’t do much for my cat unfortunately, but QVAH did and with confidence. I feel so much better now, and I’m hoping my baby does too. The whole staff is wonderful and it’s a very clean facility. Thanks again, can’t wait to bring my other cat!
Can't recommend this veterinarian enough! Wonderful facility, kind, caring and patient staff that truly want to give your pet the best possible experience!
Always friendly and helpful in taking care of our fur babies, refills for meds are pretty fast and reasonably priced, pretty easy to get an appointment even in an emergency

Dr. Greiner is the nicest, warmest, most thorough vet or doctor I've ever seen. She was so great with my human anxiety and answering all my questions. All the staff was so patient and welcoming. I really appreciate all that you do at QVAH we will always come back here! Thanks for treating my best friend so well :)

I came in to inquire about pricing… I asked about shots and spaying for my young cat,  just out of curiosity ! This snarky guy in there with glasses, at the front desk made it seem like I was stupid and poor for asking. Wouldn’t tell me how much it was and assumed I wouldn’t have the money. That alone turned me away

I can't review the Drs or the care, as I never got that far.

I had called to inquire about an ultrasound and was told that I can schedule one when necessary.

When I called back to schedule, I was told that I had to make an initial appointment and then schedule an additional imaging appointment.

When I asked if we can schedule both at the same time i was told that was not how they schedule the appointments.

After stating that I had already called and was told that I can schedule directly, I was told to contact Penn or VSEC.  The undue attitude that the woman gave me, on the phone, is enough to turn me off from their business and write this.

Below is a direct quote from their website that contradicts everything that the lady on the phone condescendingly told me:

"With the addition of our advanced portable ultrasound machine, what was once reserved for a visit to a specialty emergency center, is now capable to be incorporated into your pet’s general exam. For more in depth cases, full diagnostic ultrasounds with one of our full-time associates, can be arranged most days of the week either by appointment or by drop-off."

I don't understand why the attitude was warranted for a request that their website states is commonplace, even for a drop-off...
Dr. Greiner has been taking care of our rescue Sphinx's  for decades.  This is such a great place. They do a great job and are so kind!
Be ready to be charged for every single thing. A visit plus meds my dog won’t take cost $250.
We love the care our pups receive at Queen Village.
I wish they could treat humans here. Best medical practice ever.
Always a great experience and friendly providers.

Fantastic Animal Hospital! My dog has been seeing Dr. Collata since he was 3 months (and is now 3). Nothing but good things to say about this place. Makes you feel very comfortable, and you are never waiting long!

The doctors are all very friendly and knowledgeable but I am so impressed by the reception staff! Whenever we have a question about medications or our dog is feeling slightly off, we call and the staff who picks up is amazing at answering all of our questions quickly. Saves us so much stress!

Overall my experience has been decent with this vet clinic. I had one really bad visit with an unprofessional vet tech, but after complaining (on the internet, bc I was really put off), their manager called me and promised me that this was not their service standard.

I changed my review in good faith that this was a one time error.

I will say that my most recent trip was absolutely fine, but it was obvious that my review + complaint had been circulated. Kind of gave me scarlet letter vibe. Front desk person was kinda rude. Dr made comments about the last visit. And other lil things.

Not a big deal, but I do feel kind of awkward about going now, instead of "taken care of" like how the manager made me feel on the phone prior.

Either way, its the most convenient vet in town with South St. Pet Mechanic closing and I trust QVAH doctors, so I'll probably just muscle through it and remain a client lol
